transcript: Hi I'm Ben, and this week I saw Here Lies Love at the Broadway Theater and these are my thoughts! So there are 2 aspects of the show that I really wanna dive into today, one is the actual show itself, and two is the overall production. Because this show is above all else designed to be an EXPERIENCE! They completely renovated the Broadway theater, and turned it into an immersive disco club. And these immersive elements are where the show really shines. The show is staged so that the action happens all around the theater, although most of the action is taking place in that standing floor section. And the people standing on the floor are used in really interesting ways, so in one scene they may be a crowd of adoring fans, in another one they may be a mob of protesters, and I thought that this was a really interesting and unique way to use the immersive concept in a way that I hadn't really seen done before. There are also several moments throughout the show where the DJ or Imelda may ask you to get up and dance. And I know a lot of people who saw the show and hated the dancing elements. I did not mind it, but just be aware that if you go you will be asked to get up and dance at 3 different parts of the show. While I do get why people will not like those sections I do think that they're important because it forces the audience to become complicit in the story and I think that this plays into a lot of the themes of the show in terms of how fascist and dictators are able to amass power and that is through the complicitness of the masses. Going into it I wasn't really sure how tonally this show was going to approach being this fun disco show that is also about the rise of a dictator. But having now seen it live, I think that they do a really good job of blending the concept and the subject matter in really interesting ways. Which brings me to the show itself because while I think the production elements are all spectacular I think the show itself is just okay. The show is only 90 minutes, no intermission, and I do feel like the story felt rushed at times. There were definitely moments where I felt like they could have gone a little bit deeper so I think the show could be better served if it was expanded into a 2 act show. But I did think the story was engaging and well told and I appreciated that it never asked you to sympathize with Imelda and it never paints her as anything other than the villain that she is. They also do a really smart thing at the end of the show, which I won't spoil, but it reframes the story in a way that takes the focus away from Imelda and back onto the victims of her regime and the people that were fighting back and I think that was really smart and really impactful. But overall it's a super fun and unique theatrical experience, and we just don't get these types of shows on Broadway very often. So I definitely recommend checking it out if you are able to!
reasoning: Ben gives a clear recommendation despite acknowledging the show's flaws, praising the innovative immersive production while noting the story feels rushed. His enthusiasm for the unique theatrical experience and explicit recommendation ('I definitely recommend checking it out') outweigh his critiques.
